title: The costs of a health issue
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:33Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T08:14:04Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No bank point teaches the direct, indirect and intangible types of cost of a health issue; the closest, on identifying health priorities, uses cost only as one criterion for choosing priorities, which is a different idea.

draft.title: The costs of a health issue
card: A health issue costs more than the bill for treatment. Costs fall on the person, their family, employers and the community.
money spent on dealing with the issue itself, such as hospital care, medicines, GP visits and ambulance trips.
money lost because of the issue, though not spent on it directly, such as lost work, lost income and a carer taking time off.
effects that are real but hard to put a dollar value on, such as pain, stress, grief and a lower quality of life.
draft.remember: Direct costs are spent on care. Indirect costs are income and work lost. Intangible costs are felt, not priced.

a.q: Sam breaks his leg playing football and needs surgery. Which is a direct cost of his injury?
opts: The hospital bill for his surgery
The wages he loses while off work
The pain he feels in his leg
The stress his parents feel about it
a.why: A hospital bill is money spent on treating the injury, so it is a direct cost. Lost wages are tempting, but they are money lost because of the injury, not spent on treating it, so they are indirect.
a.clue: Which one is money spent on treating the injury itself?

b.q: Priya has anxiety and often misses school and her part-time job. Which of her costs is an indirect cost?
opts: The wages she loses on shifts she cannot work
The fees for her visits to a psychologist
The constant worry she feels each day
The medicine her doctor prescribes for her
b.why: Lost wages are money lost because of the issue, not spent on treating it, so they are indirect costs. Her constant worry is real, but it is hard to give a dollar value, so it is intangible. Fees and medicine are spent on care, so they are direct.
b.clue: Look for the money she loses, not the money spent on care.

a.best: The hospital bill for his surgery

b.best: The wages she loses on shifts she cannot work
